Pondicherry, India (WC V) |associated=[[Cobalt]], [[Gigabyte]], [[Calypso]], [[Manta]], [[JackPot]] (Derek Tran) |weight=242lbs (WC V) |clearance= |speed=19mph |drive= |weapons=Vertical spinner |other_names=Gold Fury (WC V) |other_entries= |power= |other_events=BattleBots Pro League (2026)}}'''Golden Fury''' is a [[Heavyweights|heavyweight]] robot designed by [[PY Roboticzs]] which applied for ''[[BattleBots]]'' [[World Championship V]] and will compete in the 2026 ''[[BattleBots Pro League]]''. Originally piloted by '''Team MYTHHADES''' of Chennai, India and called '''Gold Fury''', the robot was large and gold in color, designed to resemble a dragon. Gold Fury sported a large asymmetric [[Vertical Spinners|vertical spinner]] with two claw-shaped wedgelets at the front to guide opponents into the path of its primary weapon. The team uploaded an application video in January 2020 showcasing their design.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oeM8TkAslxI Team MYTHHADES for Battlebots] However, they ultimately had to withdraw their application and were not part of the original roster of competitors revealed before World Championship V's postponement due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Team MYTHHADES are not known to have applied for the two World Championships which followed. Almost six years later, the most recent version of Golden Fury was invited as one of 24 robots to compete in the 2026 ''BattleBots Pro League''. Armed with an [[Eggbeater Spinners|eggbeater weapon]], this design is an evolution of that which has fought in Russian and UAE heavyweight events. File:Gold fury 2020.png|Gold Fury as it appeared in its World Championship V application. ==Outside BattleBots== Under the name '''Golden Fury''', the robot would eventually compete at the Russian event ''Bitva Robotov'' in October 2023, appearing in the second group of qualifiers. It was reasonably successful, knocking out [[Omniwheels|mecanum]]-wheeled pneumatic spearbot '''Red Alert''' before losing by knockout to eggbeater spinner '''Daddy Bot''', eliminating Golden Fury from the qualifying rounds. Golden Fury was not selected as a wildcard, meaning their tournament ended there. The robot featured a orange fish-scale like paint job, as well as more conventional front wedge and ear designs. The team also shared no overlapping team members with those listed in their 2020 ''BattleBots'' application. Golden Fury returned to ''Bitva Robotov'' in 2024, rebuilt from its previous iteration. It defeated both '''Vacuum''' and '''Weber 4.0''' in its qualifiers, but lost to '''Iron Scrap''' in the 2024 Finals. In 2025, Golden Fury again competed at ''Bitva Robotov'' but lost its first battle to Brazil's [[Black Dragon]]. It then took on '''Star Platinum''' and '''Red Miller'''. Later in the year, Golden Fury entered the international ''Games of the Future'' event held in Abu Dhabi. In Round 1, Gold Fury took on British competitor [[w:c:robotwars:Team Toon#TR4|TR4]]. However, pre-fight issues meant Golden Fury started smoking and the fight was postponed to Day 2. On the second day, Golden Fury managed to dominate TR4, bending up its front forks and exposing the gas canister for its flipper. It was later revealed that shrapnel had breached the arena, putting a premature end to the day's battles. Golden Fury lost its next battle against '''Daddy''' and was subsequently eliminated. Golden Fury has been registered to the 2026 ''Bitva Robotov'' competition. Golden_Fury_GOTF_2025.png|Golden Fury at ''Games of the Future'' in December 2025. '''Golden Fury vs. DeathRoll'''

Golden Fury made its ''BattleBots'' debut in the first episode of 2026 ''Pro League''. In an all-international affair, it first faced off against [[Team DeathRoll|Steven Martin]] and [[DeathRoll]] in [[BattleBots Pro League/Episode 1|Episode 1]]. The team opted for their long forks with angled wedges at the tips to get underneath DeathRoll and feed it into its weapon.

[[File:Golden Fury DeathRoll Pro League 1.png|left|thumb|Golden Fury spins to face DeathRoll.]]Both robots approached the center of the [[BattleBox]], narrowly avoiding a head-on collision before they turned to face one another again. Golden Fury then charged, taking a minor hit to its side as it swept past the Australian bot, trying to bait the [[World Championship IV|2019 season]] semi-finalist into a mistake.

[[File:Golden Fury DeathRoll Pro League 2.gif|thumb|The first big hit of the fight.]]Golden Fury's eggbeater then made contact with Deathroll's disk, causing both robots to fly to opposite sides of the arena. Golden Fury was quick to recover, but this big impact broke a solder wire lug on the weapon switch[https://discord.com/channels/651601084019900483/809971550937808926/1522378597191516301 Public message in the NHRL Discord server by Derek Tran], resulting in the Indian machine's eggbeater stopping. However, DeathRoll was propelled into the [[screws]] and landed upside-down, bobbling across the BattleBox floor and ultimately falling onto its wheels.

[[File:Golden Fury DeathRoll Pro League 3.png|left|thumb|Golden Fury remains aggressive, despite losing power to its weapon.]]Despite DeathRoll's weapon still being active, Golden Fury's team were undeterred and maintained their aggression and used their ground game attachments to shepherd DeathRoll into the screws. {{Dialogue a-b|Chris Rose|And Kenny, is it possible that Golden Fury is using DeathRoll's weapon against them?|Kenny Florian|Yeah, I think that's exactly what they're doing.|Chris and Kenny pick up on Golden Fury's strategy}} [[File:Golden Fury DeathRoll Pro League 4.gif|thumb|DeathRoll is sent spiraling onto the Upper Deck.]]DeathRoll's blade made contact with Golden Fury's inactive eggbeater again, causing Steven Martin's bot to bounce uncontrollably in the short corner, before another impact saw it deflect onto the [[Upper Deck]]. DeathRoll wasted little time in escaping the hazard, chipping away one of Golden Fury's ears upon landing in the opposite corner.

[[File:Golden Fury DeathRoll pin Pro League.png|left|thumb|Golden Fury pins DeathRoll in the short corner.]]Golden Fury then maneuvered to the back end of DeathRoll, sliding its forks underneath and pinning it against the Upper Deck. It then breached the side of DeathRoll, slamming it into the opposite wall. DeathRoll had lost all of its weapon belts by this point, meaning neither robot had a functioning spinner as the battle approached the 1:00 mark.

[[File:Golden Fury DeathRoll Pro League JD.gif|thumb|Golden Fury's last attack before the clock hits zero.]]With thirty seconds remaining, Golden Fury began producing minor smoke, as noticed by [[Chris Rose]] in commentary. However, it was still able to drive DeathRoll into the arena wall twice more before time ran out.

A split judges' decision was announced, with [[Bil Dwyer]] and [[Fon Davis]] casting votes in favor of Golden Fury and DeathRoll respectively. Judge [[Pete Abrahamson]] voted in favor of Golden Fury, confirming a first win in ''BattleBots'' for PY Roboticzs. |- |
